summary: A1 overall, balanced across skills. Priority: reliable simple past tense, copula 'be' in present tense, and moving from recognition to confident production of basic vocabulary. Goal-aligned focus on travel and everyday-life topics throughout.

goals.short_term_3_6_months: Reach solid A2: introduce yourself fluently, handle past-tense narration of daily events, order food/ask directions/check into a hotel without hesitation, control present tense (incl. 'to be') reliably.
goals.medium_term_6_12_months: Consolidate A2, begin B1: hold 5+ minute unscripted conversations, write short travel-related emails/messages, understand slow-to-moderate authentic audio (announcements, simple podcasts).
goals.long_term_12_plus_months: Reach B1: handle most travel situations independently (per CEFR B1 descriptor), narrate past experiences fluently, understand routine spoken interactions with native speakers at a natural-ish pace.

time_estimate.note: These are FSI/SLA-research-based estimates for languages of moderate distance from Ukrainian. Consistency matters more than intensity: 30-45 min daily will outperform sporadic long sessions. Adding passive immersion (English audio/video during commute, travel apps) can meaningfully shorten this without adding formal session time.
time_estimate.source: cefr-framework.md quick reference table + milestones.md A1->A2/A2->B1 sections

breakdown.core_session: 20-30 min (langtutor-session, rotate types: conversation simulation and grammar-in-context prioritized early to fix past-tense/copula gaps)
breakdown.note: Four Strands balance target over a week, not every single day: ~35% meaning-focused input, ~35% meaning-focused output, ~15% language-focused (grammar/vocab), ~15% fluency drills.

priority_grammar_focus: Present tense of 'to be' (am/is/are) - currently inconsistent
Simple past tense, regular and top ~15 irregular verbs (was/were, went, had, did, ate, saw)
priority_vocabulary_focus: Travel domain: airport, hotel, directions, transportation, money/prices
Food and dining domain: ordering, menu items, dietary preferences
Numbers, time, dates (building on existing counting knowledge)

listening: Very slow, clear beginner podcasts (e.g. VOA Learning English style)
Children's/graded audio before authentic native-speed content
reading: A1 graded readers and interlinear texts via langtutor-immersion
Simple travel blogs once at A2
immersion_topics: Daily routine narration (fixes past tense gap directly)
Kam'ianets-Podilskyi-to-abroad travel scenarios for personal relevance

milestones.name: A1 -> A2 Transition
canDos: Introduce self and answer personal questions without hesitation
Reliably use present tense of 'to be' (am/is/are)
Narrate 3+ past actions using correct simple past tense
Order food and ask for the bill in a restaurant scenario
Ask for and understand basic directions
milestones.grammar_target: Present tense (all persons, incl. 'to be'), simple past tense, basic questions/negation

milestones.name: A2 -> B1 Transition
canDos: Hold 5+ minute conversations about travel plans and daily life
Write a 100-150 word message describing a trip or plan
Understand main points of simple travel-related audio/announcements
Handle unexpected turns in routine conversations (delays, mix-ups while traveling)
milestones.grammar_target: All simple tenses, basic conditionals, relative clauses, modal verbs

pipeline_notes.langtutor_session: Use for interactive practice; prioritize Grammar-in-Context (past tense, 'to be') and Conversation Simulation (travel/restaurant scenarios) for the first several sessions.
pipeline_notes.langtutor_vocab: Start with top 300-500 frequency words plus travel/food domains; daily SRS review.
pipeline_notes.langtutor_tracker: Check in weekly to confirm skill balance and milestone progress against this plan.
pipeline_notes.langtutor_immersion: Generate travel- and daily-life-themed reading passages and scenario cards to keep motivation tied to the stated goal.
